items.headline: Democrats clinch largest House majority since 1992
items.summary: Democrats have won at least 258 of 435 House seats, their largest majority since 1992, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina. Four races remain undecided, including two Louisiana seats headed to a December runoff.

items.headline: U.N. climate talks collapse over fossil fuels
items.summary: Nearly 200 countries meeting at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, ended without agreeing on whether to move away from fossil fuels, the main driver of global warming. Delegates said they could not accept a draft that lacked fossil fuel language, and disputes over funding were left unresolved.

items.headline: Ukraine says drones sank Russian warship in Libya
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says sea drones struck and sank a Russian navy vessel docked at a naval base in Libya. He described the strike as a surprise attack.

items.headline: Spy chief defends Trump calling Putin a 'friend'
items.summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said President Trump's description of Vladimir Putin as a friend was "entirely appropriate," after a rare three-way summit in China with Putin and Xi Jinping that Democrats criticized. Clayton added that Putin is not America's friend in Ukraine.

items.headline: Appeals court strikes down pregnant-worker law
items.summary: The 5th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 9-8 that the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act is unconstitutional because most House members were not physically present when it passed under pandemic-era proxy voting. Advocates say the ruling voids the law in Texas, Louisiana and Mississippi and expect an appeal to the Supreme Court.

items.headline: Delta system failure delays two-thirds of flights
items.summary: A problem with an automation system that calculates aircraft weight delayed about 1,000 Delta flights, or 67%, by Sunday afternoon and led to an FAA ground stop for some flights into Atlanta. Delta later said the system was working again as Thanksgiving travel picked up.

items.headline: ICE arrests at Seattle airport draw criticism
items.summary: Immigration officers detained two people on a jet bridge at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, delaying an Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles. Alaska Airlines said it got no advance notice, and Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson called the tactics "deeply un-American."

items.headline: Israeli troops pull back from Lebanese village
items.summary: Residents of a southern Lebanese village returned home after Israeli forces withdrew and the Lebanese army took over. Many found their houses badly damaged.

items.headline: Grocery prices cloud Thanksgiving meal costs
items.summary: Rising grocery prices make the cost of this year's Thanksgiving meal uncertain, according to food-price analysts. Some people are hosting fewer guests or skipping hosting altogether.

items.headline: Older drivers lean on Tesla's automated driving
items.summary: Older drivers are relying on Tesla's automated driving features to keep driving longer. Safety experts question whether the company overstates what the technology can do.

digest.overview:
Democrats have locked in at least 258 House seats, their largest majority since 1992, after Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton called President Trump's description of Vladimir Putin as a "friend" "entirely appropriate" after a rare three-way summit with Putin and Xi Jinping in China. A federal appeals court ruled 9-8 that the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act is unconstitutional because most House members were absent under proxy voting when it passed. A system failure delayed about two-thirds of Delta's flights on Sunday and prompted an FAA ground stop in Atlanta as Thanksgiving travel ramped up. Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson called ICE arrests on a Seattle airport jet bridge "deeply un-American." The Army plans to detonate several tons of degraded lead azide in Iowa by Tuesday despite a court hold.

Abroad, U.N. climate talks in Turkey collapsed after nearly 200 countries split over whether to phase away from fossil fuels. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said sea drones sank a Russian navy vessel docked in Libya, while a Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih killed two people and wounded 60. A Kaliningrad-bound Russian cargo ship caught fire in the Gulf of Finland after a drone hit. Denmark expelled Russia's defense attaché over an alleged plot to kill a Ukrainian American rapper, and Poland said it foiled a separate attempt. Mexico flew cartel leader "El Chapo Isidro" to Mexico City after a Sinaloa shootout that left at least 11 dead. The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission entered orbit around Mercury, the first visit to the planet in more than a decade.

home.overview:
Brock Purdy threw three first-half touchdown passes as the 49ers crushed the Vikings 35–10 in Mexico City to reach 9-1, and Dallas scored on its first six drives in a 51–30 rout of Tennessee. Carolina outlasted Baltimore 35–33, Philadelphia snapped a seven-game skid against Pittsburgh, and Denver now leads the AFC West over Kansas City on a tiebreaker. Detroit lost Aidan Hutchinson for the season, and the Bengals visit Washington tonight before a Thanksgiving slate of Bears–Lions, Eagles–Cowboys and Chiefs–Bills. In the NBA, Jamal Murray's 45 points carried Denver past Chicago 151–145 in overtime, and Miami won its seventh straight. Baseball's offseason got its headline: Tarik Skubal to the Mets for a reported nine years and $450 million.

Liverpool thrashed 10-man Man United 4–0 to spoil Mauricio Pochettino's debut, while Hull's late double sank Brighton and left Arsenal six points clear. Barcelona rallied from 2–0 down to beat Villarreal 3–2, Werder Bremen routed Hamburg 4–0, and Bayern lost Harry Kane for months. The Champions League returns Tuesday with Arsenal–Dortmund and Man City–Napoli. Cincinnati stunned Nashville in MLS Round One, and FC Seoul host Daejeon in K League 1's penultimate round. In the KBO, Hanwha signed Jesse Scholtens ahead of Thursday's MVP awards.

fact.answer:
Every popcorn kernel holds a little water inside a core of soft, starchy endosperm, sealed in a very hard outer shell. Heated to about 400°F (200°C), that water turns to steam, and the pressure builds until the shell bursts. The starch inflates and the kernel turns inside out into a fluffy white puff roughly 20 to 40 times its original size.

Not just any corn will do: only about 25 types are suited to popping. Long before the physics was understood, some Native American tribes explained the pop as angry spirits inside each kernel escaping as steam when heated.

The takeaway: popping depends on the water inside, so kernels need to keep a certain moisture level.
